title: Property Tax Procedure
outcome: Walk ordinary assessment protest, payment-under-protest or refund, and redemption paths with the correct local filings.
source_notebooks: The Unconfused Man and his Person

steps.title: Read the assessment or tax notice carefully

lines.text: Identify the parcel or account number, assessed value, tax year, protest deadline, and the board or office named on the notice.

speed_bumps: Deadlines are often short and may require filing with a specific county board rather than the collector.

steps.title: File a written valuation protest when available

forms.title: Written Protest of Valuation (local board form)

lines.text: State the parcel, the assessed value you dispute, and the factual basis for a lower value or unequal treatment, then keep a filed-stamped copy.

speed_bumps: Some jurisdictions require payment of the undisputed amount, or payment under protest, before a refund path opens.

delivery.method: File with the board or office named on the notice
delivery.destination: County board of equalization / tax assessor as stated locally

steps.title: Use pay-under-protest or refund procedures when required

forms.title: Petition for Tax Refund / Payment Under Protest

lines.text: Where the statute requires payment first, pay under protest as instructed, then petition for refund with proof of payment and the protest basis.

speed_bumps: Federal courts often defer to state tax remedies if a plain, speedy, and efficient state path exists.

steps.title: Map tax-sale redemption or purchase rights

forms.title: Application to Redeem Land Sold for Taxes (state/county form)

lines.text: Confirm whether the land was sold or bid in, the redemption period, who must be paid, and which office issues a certificate of redemption.

evidence_hooks.ref: Alabama Code Title 40 Chapter 10 (example jurisdictional map — confirm your state)

speed_bumps: Redemption amounts, notice rules, and who holds the certificate vary by state and sale type.

delivery.method: Application to the probate judge, land commissioner, or tax collecting official as statute requires
delivery.destination: County office named in the applicable tax-sale chapter

steps.title: Inventory non-recognized tax-bill discharge theories separately

lines.text: Theories that treat a local tax bill stub as a negotiable instrument that forces Treasury settlement are contested and are not ordinary property-tax procedure.

speed_bumps: Do not substitute an unverified endorsement protocol for protest, payment, or redemption filings the collecting office accepts.
flags: IRM and related materials screen frivolous and fictitious-instrument submissions; inventory only — not a recommended playbook.
